messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> SEV2: runtime-high-error-rate triggered for service 'redwood-runtime' at 2026-03-14T02:13:09Z. Paging matt.ops (ops oncall) and carla.sre. Bridge: https://bridge.redwood.com/xyz

matt.ops: joining bridge now. I see initial spike in 02:12-02:14 UTC. Oncall context: high 5xxs on /v1/generate and elevated latency for dedicated pools.

alice.eng: I'm awake, joining. Any customer-facing impact visibility?

sara.support: We have two enterprise customers reporting timeouts and a few alerts from health-checks. CS is on it, sending list of impacted customer IDs in a sec.

carla.sre: brief plan: (1) collect timeline/primary logs (2) identify hypothesis (3) mitigation (fallback/canary) (4) comms/statuspage. I'm going to be the scribe for the timeline unless someone else volunteers.

carla.sre: Scribe notes start:
- 02:12:31 UTC: spike in gen latency detected by alert rule runtime_err_rate (threshold 0.5%)
- 02:12:45 UTC: first customer timeout (cust: corp-acme)
- 02:13:09 UTC: PD page triggered (SEV2)
- 02:14:05 UTC: initial bridge created
- 02:16:10 UTC: support reports 3 distinct customers affected

matt.ops: I'm capturing pod-level events and kernel logs. Attaching quick grep of kube logs for "OOM" from the serving nodes:

```
Mar 14 02:12:33 node-gpu-07 kernel: oom-killer: Killed process 14231 (redwood-serving) total-vm:1023456kB, anon-rss:456792kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
Mar 14 02:12:34 node-gpu-07 redwood-serving[14231]: ERROR kv-cache: allocation failed: insufficient memory
Mar 14 02:12:35 node-gpu-07 redwood-serving[14231]: WARN fallback: switching to unquantized kernel
```

deepak.infra: I'm seeing node memory pressure on gpu-07 and gpu-09 around the same time. Recently pushed a kernel patch yesterday but that shouldn't affect runtime memory layout. Posting dmesg and pod env in the bridge.

alice.eng: hypothesis A: KV cache growth + allocator bug triggered by certain long-context requests -> OOM and process restarts causing 5xxs. Hypothesis B: kernel/user-space mismatch after yesterday's host kernel update -> memory accounting drift.

kernel-bot: Kernel mismatch check: host kernel version 6.1.19 (updated 2026-03-13 23:50 UTC) vs expected 6.1.18. No auto-rollbacks detected.

carla.sre: let's track hypotheses inline:
- H1 (kv-growth): reproducer: heavy long-context batch; evidence: kv-cache OOM logs, warnings about fallback
- H2 (kernel mismatch): reproducer: process memory accounting drift after host update; evidence: kernel-bot reporting version mismatch and oom-killer entries
- H3 (model compile/kernels): reproducer: specific model variant + quantization path triggers blob growth; evidence: logs show "switching to unquantized kernel" and increased RSS after compile

jon.pm: For comms: draft statuspage text (please edit) ->
```
We are investigating increased error rates and timeouts for the text-generation endpoints. Impact: partial degradation affecting a subset of customers. Engineers are diagnosing root cause. Next update: in 30 minutes. P0 owner: matt.ops.
```

carla.sre: action items (assigning):
- matt.ops: collect full dmesg + pod restart traces from gpu-07/09 and upload to /incidents/1982456789/logs (ETA 10m)
- alice.eng: run isolated reproducer on staging with long-context prompts (ETA 20m)
- deepak.infra: check node kernel rollout history and confirm whether any nodes have kernel 6.1.19 (ETA 5m)
- jon.pm & sara.support: prepare customer outreach list and initial statuspage draft (ETA 15m)
- carla.sre: maintain timeline + hypothesis table and own comm cadence (ETA immediate)

matt.ops: uploading logs now: https://internal-redwood/s3/incidents/1982456789/raw-logs.tar.gz. Notable: two process restarts from oom-killer between 02:12:33-02:12:37 on gpu-07.

alice.eng: reproduced in staging with a batch of 24 long-context requests hitting kv-cache hot-path. Memory climbs steadily and then triggers allocation failure after ~90s. Attaching snippet:
```
[staging] 2026-03-14T02:28:12Z model-serving: kv-cache size 1.2G -> 1.9G -> allocation failed
[staging] 2026-03-14T02:30:05Z trace: compile path: quantize->jit-kernel-fallback
```

carla.sre: With repro confirming kv-growth, priority mitigation: limit kv-cache growth and apply config to cap per-request kv allocation on serving nodes. Also prepare fast fallback: route heavy long-context customers to a lower-memory model variant (reduces quality but restores availability).

deepak.infra: rolling a kube config change to set memory.limit for serving pods to force OOM earlier and let autoscaler spin new pods rather than letting host oom-killer kill whole process. Rolling to gpu-07 only as canary (02:45 UTC).

jon.pm: I'll send statuspage update now with impacted customer list removed and general language. Draft: "We're investigating elevated error rates on our text-generation endpoints. Some customers may experience timeouts or increased latency. Engineers are working on mitigations; next update in 30 minutes." Any objections? :eyes:

sara.support: go ahead. CS ready to send targeted messages to impacted customers with mitigation steps and mitigations timeline.

matt.ops: mitigation applied to gpu-07 canary. Monitoring for 5 minutes. If stable, we'll roll to gpu-09.

carla.sre: decisions recorded in timeline: applied resource-limits canary 02:45 UTC, routing fallback policy staged 02:52 UTC (for enterprise corp-acme), preparing post-incident RCA template.

jon.pm: comms sequence assigned:
- 02:30 UTC (jon.pm): initial public statuspage update -> done
- 03:00 UTC (jon.pm + sara.support): targeted customer notifications (CS)
- 04:00 UTC (carla.sre): follow-up update with root-cause hypothesis and mitigation status

matt.ops: handing over live bridge to night oncall (dawn.ops) at 03:15 UTC. my notes: see /incidents/1982456789/hand-off.md.

carla.sre: scribe closing note: continue to capture post-mitigation metrics for 2h, collect heapdumps from any process OOMing, and include kernel version checks in RCA. I'll own the RCA draft. Please add any missing logs to the S3 path.

jon.pm: thanks all. tagging execs: @alice.eng @deepak.infra for visibility. We'll reconvene if the canary shows regressions.

incident-bot: Incident update logged: SEV2 -> ongoing. Thread archived for timeline assembly (do not delete)."
